Sentence (English): My first impression when opening the box for this dishwasher is that Maytag is getting it's act together.
Comments (English): [ Good first impression but very loud ] || ---------------- || My first impression when opening the box for this dishwasher is that Maytag is getting it's act together. Off the cuff, it's a good design. A lot of engineering clearly went into fit, form, and function. A huge improvement over past dishwashers that were basically a vertical cooler with plumbing parts attached. Despite the good, I could also see right away where corners were cut. Racks are flimsy, metal is thin, and seals seem a bit sketchy but only time will tell. Also, my last dishwasher was a Kenmore and and was whisper quiet. It had a huge, insulated macerating motor that the only way you knew it was running is by the gentle splashing of the spraybar. This unit has a very small motor, and in comparison, makes a very noticeable humming. Anyway, I can hear the dishwasher from two rooms away so the quiet decibel rating on this dishwasher has to be a joke. At the end of the day, the bar to take the title of "best dishwasher" is low, very low. This simply has to clean better and last longer than the Kenmore, which started malfunctioning little more two years into it. But not surprising, as my model of Kenmore was and is a known disaster. If you have had one, you know what I'm talking about. the dreaded malfunctioning motherboard and spontaneous leaking. Who puts a non-conformal, non-sealed, delicate electronic component in a door that can fill up with hot steam? Who does that? Oh, just about all of the manufactures for over a decade, starting after 2010. $500 dishwasher. corrosion. $1000 dishwasher. corrosion. Kenmore, Whirpool, Kitchenaide. all the same. If you're one of the really unlucky ones, you got the lemon that leaked, rusted, and also failed to clean dishes. Lastly, I have it on good authority, from the mystical appliance shop owner in my city, who is as surly as the "No soup for you! " character in Seinfeld, that new Maytags are solid. That Maytag licked its wounds, and designed a dishwasher that doesn't self-destruct as a feature of it's brilliant design. Only time will tell. One more thing. Because all new dishwashers have turbidity sensors, buy some food grade citric acid powder and run a rinse cycle with a teaspoon of it. It will decalcify your heating element and also help clean the turbidity sensor. If you knew the headache you saving yourself, you'd thank me. Only 4 stars because it's way, way, too loud. Come on Maytag. for $800 you couldn't quiet this thing down a bit?

Sentence (English): Purchase detergent in advance: Since I didn't have any detergent, I was only able to use it the next day after installation.
Comments (English): [ Before the washing machine arrives, purchase detergent in advance and install it in a corner. ] || ---------------- || Purchase detergent in advance: Since I didn't have any detergent, I was only able to use it the next day after installation. If you're planning to buy, I recommend purchasing dishwasher-specific detergent in advance so you can start the day off feeling great. They give you an Ecover coupon when you come for installation, and since the welcome pack is cheap, I used the coupon and purchased my first detergent from the Ecover website. Performance: I didn't really consider the features, as I thought all modern dishwashers would clean similarly well. However, I purchased this model because I wanted a hot air dryer. After using it, I found that even with the hot air dryer, the clothes didn't come out completely dry after the dryer cycle. I ended up having to leave the dishwasher door wide open all night to get the squeaky-dry clothes out and put them in the upper cabinet in the morning. Therefore, I don't think you need to insist on a model with a hot air dryer. Installation location: 1. Installing it right next to the sink seems like a great choice. First of all, the water pipe doesn't have to be long (after all, longer pipes can cause problems), but you can also place dripping dishes without spilling too much water on the floor after pre-washing. Second, after installing, I noticed that avoid installing in a corner. If you do, it's difficult to open the lower cabinet where it meets. Dishwashers typically require doors to be open to avoid moisture, but the lower cabinet where it meets must also be opened after cooking due to the heat from the induction cooktop. This means you might forget to close the dishwasher overnight, or you might find it difficult to use the lower cabinet when drying dishes. If you have the space, I highly recommend installing the dishwasher in a middle cabinet. Mop base color: I chose Kota White for my white kitchen cabinets. The dishwasher mop base is black, so I couldn't get a perfect built-in fit. While some interior design companies offer color-coordinated mop bases, I don't want to hide the dishwasher, so I'll just stick with it. Residual detergent: There's a mode called "Top Rapid Mode," which only washes the top rack, excluding the bottom. Top Rapid seems to have weaker cleaning power. And while most dishes are clean, sometimes the dishes are slightly slippery after washing. YouTube shows that dishwashing detergent residue isn't 100% removed, so I'm going to stick with eco-friendly detergents. Installation: You'll need to drill a hole under the sink during installation, so I recommend clearing out any items under the sink beforehand. This will prevent dust from entering. The water is forced drainage, so the drain pipe is convex upwards. Conclusion: The only drawback is the installation location, not the product itself. It definitely improves your quality of life. Since everyone agrees, I won't go into detail. If I were you, I'd buy any model. I don't have to do the dishes myself!

Sentence (English): We needed a new dishwasher, after the old one became too costly to repair.
Comments (English): [ Poorly designed part ] || ---------------- || We needed a new dishwasher, after the old one became too costly to repair. We purchased this new one just in time for Christmas 2023. I installed it and did the leak check as instructed. Found a leak only coming from the left side of the machine. Found to be from the “ fill funnel”, which is open to the exterior of the dishwasher and neighboring cabinetry, and we know how cabinetry holds up to moisture. After the part was replace 2 times by a certified warranty company and continued to leak. It was finally considered “Not Repairable “. GE then attempted to replace it with an identical model, which I refused, and requested a refund. GE did refund our entire amount including tax. Thank You, GE. Sad part is, that my wife “Loved” the look, location of the controls and interior space. If it wasn't for a poorly designed “fill funnel” that allows water to have access to the exterior of the machine and your cabinetry, which can be extremely costly. The part design needs a simple fix and you'd have a great dishwasher.

Sentence (English): We bought this machine to replace our 6 year old Bosch 100 Series dishwasher because we wanted something that would clean a little better and would dry out the dishes.
Comments (English): [ Such a DIFFERENCE from our Bosch 100 Series! ] || ---------------- || We bought this machine to replace our 6 year old Bosch 100 Series dishwasher because we wanted something that would clean a little better and would dry out the dishes. Also we have an electric water heater, so the water warmer on the 100 never seemed to work very well, which caused us to have even MORE issues with cleaning! Also, our rinse dispenser never worked on that machine. that's a long story, but we tried to repair it and that didn't work. So far, REALLY IMPRESSED with this machine and we haven't even used all of its features! We had an Ascenta in our old home we were very happy with, so when we bought our new home, we thought we would be as happy with the 100 line as they had discontinued the Ascenta line. It was good and that machine is still working, but it just does not have the same capabilities. The 800 blows the 100 away! When I unloaded the dishwasher this morning, we have a juicer we use to handpress juice into foods. The oils from the rind would get on the stainless steel and be very hard to get off, even by handwashing. I noticed in putting the dishes today that the residual oils were pretty much off the inside of the squeezer! Pretty impressive! Obviously, it's cleaning abilities are awesome! What's even nicer is when opening the dishwasher in the morning, the dishes are warm which leads me to believe that the water is getting hotter now, something that did not happen with our old 100 Series. For those buyers who complain about their Bosch not drying well (especially plastics), larger plastic items do very well on the bottom shelf. I've noticed there is very little water on them when I take them out. While we use a lot of smaller containers for sauces for lunches and I do put them on the top third shelf, I just lay them on a dishmat and they dry in no time! I didn't think there could be an even QUIETER machine, but the 800 series is even quieter than our 100 was. I recommend if your budget allows it to buy the higher end machine. My husband was very impressed with the plug and play aspect of the machine installation. I think the only part he really had an issue with was the levelers/legs in the front. Having said that, this machine went in much faster than our old Bosch! As this is our third Bosch machine, we have had other dishwashers over the years. In 43 years of marriage, we have owned five machines total. The first two roughed up most of my dishes terribly causing chips in the glaze and the racks of them would rust through eventually causing the dishes to be exposed to that. None of my Bosch machines have ever done that. Buying a Bosch machine means you are buying a dishwasher, not a dishblaster! It's gentle, yet it does the job of cleaning! Very happy with the new machine!

Comments (English): [ The technician was very kind and did a good job installing it. ] || ---------------- || This is an actual review after 3 months of use. I was planning to buy a 12-person dishwasher when I get my own house, and I am very satisfied that I was able to install it after the construction. It washes the dishes very cleanly, and it comes out dried, so I can just store it in the upper cabinet, which is very convenient. For dishes with a lot of food stuck to them, you can add steam. Pans with black seasoning stuck to them after grilling meat also come out cleanly. I hate having food stuck to the filter, so I just rinse it in water and put it in. This is not a preliminary dishwashing. I just roughly rinse the food with water. Even just doing that makes filter cleaning much easier.

Sentence (English): We bought this machine to replace our 6 year old Bosch 100 Series dishwasher because we wanted something that would clean a little better and would dry out the dishes.
Comments (English): [ Such a DIFFERENCE from our Bosch 100 Series! ] || ---------------- || We bought this machine to replace our 6 year old Bosch 100 Series dishwasher because we wanted something that would clean a little better and would dry out the dishes. Also we have an electric water heater, so the water warmer on the 100 never seemed to work very well, which caused us to have even MORE issues with cleaning! Also, our rinse dispenser never worked on that machine. that's a long story, but we tried to repair it and that didn't work. So far, REALLY IMPRESSED with this machine and we haven't even used all of its features! We had an Ascenta in our old home we were very happy with, so when we bought our new home, we thought we would be as happy with the 100 line as they had discontinued the Ascenta line. It was good and that machine is still working, but it just does not have the same capabilities. The 800 blows the 100 away! When I unloaded the dishwasher this morning, we have a juicer we use to handpress juice into foods. The oils from the rind would get on the stainless steel and be very hard to get off, even by handwashing. I noticed in putting the dishes today that the residual oils were pretty much off the inside of the squeezer! Pretty impressive! Obviously, it's cleaning abilities are awesome! What's even nicer is when opening the dishwasher in the morning, the dishes are warm which leads me to believe that the water is getting hotter now, something that did not happen with our old 100 Series.For those buyers who complain about their Bosch not drying well (especially plastics), larger plastic items do very well on the bottom shelf. I've noticed there is very little water on them when I take them out. While we use a lot of smaller containers for sauces for lunches and I do put them on the top third shelf, I just lay them on a dishmat and they dry in no time! I didn't think there could be an even QUIETER machine, but the 800 series is even quieter than our 100 was. I recommend if your budget allows it to buy the higher end machine.My husband was very impressed with the plug and play aspect of the machine installation. I think the only part he really had an issue with was the levelers/legs in the front. Having said that, this machine went in much faster than our old Bosch! As this is our third Bosch machine, we have had other dishwashers over the years. In 43 years of marriage, we have owned five machines total. The first two roughed up most of my dishes terribly causing chips in the glaze and the racks of them would rust through eventually causing the dishes to be exposed to that. None of my Bosch machines have ever done that. Buying a Bosch machine means you are buying a dishwasher, not a dishblaster! It's gentle, yet it does the job of cleaning! Very happy with the new machine!

Sentence (English): The best thing about the dishwasher is that it doesn't make a sound even on normal programs (and it still has another extra quiet one for the nights).

Thanks to the fact that it has a light projected on the ground, we know that it is running, otherwise it would be impossible. We love the 1-hour program, it is the one we use the most and despite being so short, everything is very clean and dry. The operation is very simple, which we appreciate, each button serves one thing, you don't have to go through the screen or anything strange. To add a drawback to improve, the red grip area of the upper tray is inserted about 2cm inwards, it could have been straight.
Comments (Original): [ Silencio absoluto ] || ---------------- || Lo mejor del lavaplatos es que no hace ni un ruido ni siquiera en los programas normales (y todavía tiene otro extrasilencioso para las noches). Gracias a que lleva una luz proyectada en el suelo, sabemos que está en marcha que si no sería imposible. El programa de 1h nos encanta, es el que más usamos y pese a ser tan corto queda todo bien limpio y seco. El manejo es muy sencillo, lo cual agradecemos, cada botón sirve para una cosa, no hay que ir pasando de pantalla ni nada raro. Por poner una pega a mejorar, la zona de agarre color rojo de la bandeja superior se mete unos 2cm hacia dentro, podría haber sido recta.

Sentence (English): I love this washer.
Comments (English): [ Great dishwasher, some minor wishes ] || ---------------- || I love this washer. Crystal dry is great. I had the Bosch 300 before and this one cleans better and dries better. HOWEVER, the prior one had push buttons, this one has touch. The touch buttons are hard to press at times. Also, I'm finding sometimes I'll be on one wash setting, but it doesn't let me switch to another one. I'll press speed 60, but then realize I have time for more, so I'll switch to normal. It won't let me on the dishwasher. It'll let me if I do it through the app though. Weird. Also, crystal dry only work with normal washes, not with speed 60 or quick washes, which isn't the end of the world, but feels like you get this great feature but can't use it in all instances. Otherwise, great dishwasher in everything I'm sure you've already read positive about this thing, including the sound, cleaning power, etc.

Sentence (English): I purchased the WHIRLPOOL Dishwasher a few months ago with high hopes of streamlining my kitchen chores.
Comments (English): [ Decent Performance with Room for Improvement ] || ---------------- || I purchased the WHIRLPOOL Dishwasher a few months ago with high hopes of streamlining my kitchen chores. Overall, I've found it to be a reliable appliance that gets the job done efficiently. However, there's one glaring issue that I can't ignore – its drying capabilities.In terms of washing, the WHIRLPOOL Dishwasher performs admirably. It effectively removes stains and grime, leaving dishes sparkling clean. Unfortunately, where the WHIRLPOOL Dishwasher falls short is in its drying function. Despite selecting the Extended Dry option, I consistently find that dishes come out damp or even wet. This is disappointing, especially considering the additional time and energy spent on the extended drying cycle. It's frustrating to have to hand-dry dishes after they've supposedly gone through a drying cycle.While the dishwasher's washing performance meets my expectations, the lackluster drying function diminishes its overall effectiveness. I've experimented with different loading configurations and drying settings, but the results remain consistent – damp dishes that require manual drying.In conclusion, the WHIRLPOOL Dishwasher is a decent appliance that excels in washing dishes but falters in drying them effectively. If drying performance is a priority for you, it might be worth exploring other options on the market. However, if you're willing to overlook this flaw or don't mind hand-drying dishes, the WHIRLPOOL Dishwasher still offers value with its reliable cleaning capabilities.

Sentence (English): There wasn't a display model at Lowe's, but the reviews were so glowing about its capacity and the pictures seemed to be OK, but this is by far the worst-designed dishwasher I have ever seen.
Comments (English): [ If you like to cook, don't buy this dishwasher ] || ---------------- || There wasn't a display model at Lowe's, but the reviews were so glowing about its capacity and the pictures seemed to be OK, but this is by far the worst-designed dishwasher I have ever seen.Yes, it may fit a lot of plates, but it hardly holds any pots and pans due to the design on the lowest rack. Some examples:-Have 11x17 jelly roll pans? Forget it. They're too high - the wash arm under the second rack would hit them. 11 x 17 is a bog-standard size. Ditto for a cutting board the same size. So much for sanitizing a cutting board.-A standard size pancake turner won't fit in the utensil drawer. When in the lying down position, it's too tall,-Serving pasta in bowls? Well, you can fit five of them, but forget being able to wash the pans in which you made the pasta and sauce or anything else.-Want to roast a turkey? Get ready to wash your roaster by hand - it won't fit.-Basically, you can wash plates or pans, but not both. This is absurd. I've never had or seen a dishwasher with such a terrible lower rack design.I was kind of hoping that when I got this dishwasher that I could give up washing dishes by hand. It's not a difficult expectation. I was wrong. Very wrong.I certainly don't have the funds to buy a replacement. The design flaws are so elementary that I'm shocked this dishwasher even made it to the market. It's also annoying that I had to pay for a power cord because one was actually included.I'm known in my community as the resident chef, and people enjoy my dinner parties, and baked goods (and other items) that I bring to potlucks and get-togethers. For a lot of people I'm their got-to guy when it comes to asking about kitchen tools and appliances.I will be sure to tell them to avoid this machine like the plague.

Sentence (English): Cleans very well.
Comments (English): [ Bosch 800 series Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || Cleans very well. I was skeptical at first. I like to rinse off my dishes and scrub off any tough cooked on gunck. But I have loaded up some fairly messy dishes and it has cleaned them up. It is quiet. And the dishes come out very dry. And since there is no heating element you can load plastics in either the top or bottom rack. The rack configurations are taking a little time to get used to. My only problem with it is that there is no indicator on the machine of it's status as it is running nor when it is done. It will send me a text message, which is totally useless. I don't need to know when it is finished if I am out to dinner. But I would like to know if it is done when I walk into the kitchen. There is a light that is on while it is running. But it goes out when it is finished. Our old dishwasher had a green light that was on when it finished and stayed on until the door was opened. That was very useful.

Sentence (English): This is replacement portable dishwasher for one we had for about 20 years.
Comments (English): [ It's Halfway to Great ] || ---------------- || This is replacement portable dishwasher for one we had for about 20 years. What we love about this GE is the stainless steel inside. It does not have a drying cycle but it gets super hot inside and the stainless steel interior helps to trap the heat and dry the dishes. There are some we need to dry off but not many. It does clean the dishes and pots/pans well. We don't put things in with stuff on them. We scrape or do a quick rinse first. The biggest con is the fact you can't see the display on the outside. While it looks sleek and cool on the outside with the stainless front panel unencumbered by a display, you have to bend down and twist your neck to see the lit-up numbers inside a slit on top of where the door closes. Our other dishwasher had the display on the outside. I don't know why they did this. There is a ring noise when the cycle is done, but it's not very loud. We found that timing the cycle helps to know when it's complete. But don't let this deter you from buying this. It seems to be a well-built dishwasher that does clean dishes well, even on the light cycle.

Sentence (English): I know that Wirecutter named this the best dishwasher money can buy, but I hate it with the fire of a thousand suns.
Comments (English): [ Not the dishwasher for you if you have a baby ] || ---------------- || I know that Wirecutter named this the best dishwasher money can buy, but I hate it with the fire of a thousand suns. Specifically, I absolutely would not recommend this dishwasher if you have a baby or small children because its ability to dry plastic is very poor. So, unless you want to spend a lot of time hand-drying wet bottles, sippy cups, tupperware, or what have you, I'd look into something else. My biggest complaint with the Bosch is I felt like I couldn't fit many dishes in it. I've read that loading it takes some getting used to, but I didn't get the hang of it after three months - it seems over-optimized. My dishes also emerged still dirty more than a few times. I previously had an ancient Maytag and I ended up exchanging the Bosch for a new Maytag (Wirecutter's #2 pick) which I like much better. The one thing I will say about the Bosch is it is VERY quiet. You could barely tell it's running. But, my new dishwasher has basically the same level of noise and I can actually fit stuff in it so I don't have to run the dishwasher every day anymore. I have never returned an appliance before but this one had to go.

Sentence (English): (This review was collected as part of a promotion.)
Comments (English): [ Replacing my old SHX5ER55U dishwasher ] || ---------------- || (This review was collected as part of a promotion.) All new, all beautiful, this new modernized model has what it takes to please us like my old one. Quiet, very efficient, washes perfectly and the dishes come out sparkling and dries even pots and utensils soiled with a hard, burnt crust! My old Bosch dishwasher, 10 years old, had problems with "e:15" leaks and sometimes the detergent tablet did not dissolve or only partially dissolved. My wife didn't want me to spend a penny to have it looked at by a technician and repaired and wanted to replace it instead. After research and investigation I understood that the source of the problems we had with the old one ultimately came from the misuse of our dishwasher which impaired its performance, disrupted its washing cycle because of the dishes always well rinsed (under penalty of harsh reprimands from my partner!) that we put in them (yes, find out the reasons that the manufacturer and the Finish detergent company advise you not to rinse the dishes before putting them in the dishwasher) and shortcomings in its installation in the plumbing for the water drain which was not done well. I know that now because my new dishwasher reacts the same with water remaining inside the filter and since it is brand new, I know that it is not the dishwasher that is faulty! I also made a service call to the administration of my building so that their plumber could come back and redo the job of installing the water drain which he did not install exactly as the Bosch guide shows. . Now I have taken back control of managing the dishes intended for the dishwasher and don't let anyone rinse their dishes before putting them in the dishwasher! And I hold my own, whether the girls and women in the house (I'm the only man) shun me (out of pride) or not!
Comments (Original): [ Remplacement de mon vieux lave-vaisselle SHX5ER55U ] || ---------------- || (This review was collected as part of a promotion.) Tout nouveau, tout beau, ce nouveau modèle modernisé à ce qu'il faut pour nous plaire comme mon ancien. J'ai d'ailleurs fait un appel de service à l'administration de mon immeuble pour que leur plombier revienne refaire la job d'installation du renvois d'eau qu'il n'a pas installé exactement comme le guide de Bosch le montre.  Maintenant j'ai repris le contrôle de la gestion de la vaisselle destiné au lave-vaisselle et ne laisse personne rincer sa vaisselle avant de la mettre au lave-vaisselle! Et je tiens mon bout, que les filles et femmes de la maison (j'suis le seul homme) me boudent (par orgueil)ou non!

When I explained the situation to the associate who took my call, he was clearly unaware of someone would be coming in for the haul away for us on 12/26/23. I didn't hear back from the store, but I received an email from their installation scheduling team saying that our dishwasher installation + haul away appointment is scheduled to 1/10/24!! I didn't know what happened to my original 12/29/23 appointment, but 1/10/24 was unacceptable because we were hosting a New Year's Eve party. How could we have a new dishwasher sitting in the middle of my dining room! Also the associate who promised to take care of my transferring the haul away request never told me that this would mean I had to give up the appointment on the 29th and to make a new one. If I were informed, I would still go with the installation on 29th, and then had Lowe's people to come haul away the old one. All these phone calls, we still ended up losing the chance to install the new dishwasher on 29th. Due to my own schedule, I later changed the installation + haul away appointment from 1/10/24 to 1/19/24. It didn't matter much any more after we hosted the party with a new dishwasher in my dining room. I got things out and cleared cabinet space again to prepare for installation. On 1/19/24, an installer came. He looked pretty experienced and professional. When he looked at our space, he immediately said that we need a 4-ft drain hose extension in order to reach the drain. He also pointed out the power cord is for Bosch, not LG, but cord in the dishwasher should work with our existing outlet and we don't need any external power cord. In the end, he could not install for us because we didn't have the drain hose extension. He told us to call again to reschedule when we got the extension. We spent days online and going to different stores to look for a 4-ft drain hose extension. There is no such thing as 4-ft drain hose extension!! The shortest is 6-ft! We got a bunch of different hoses and hose extensions, and finally rescheduled the appointment to 2/3/24. I contacted the contracting company to make sure the hoses we got would work, not like the 19th. It was good that the contracting company moved our appointment up to 1/30/24. Finally an installer came and installed the new dishwasher on the 30th. He pointed out the dishwasher connector that Lowe's bundled and delivered to us was much bigger for our LG dishwasher!!! Thank God he was able to use the connector from the old dishwasher. He used the 6-ft drain hose extension. Although there is a little U shape, I was able to fix it myself later. Finally and finally, we have our new LG dishwasher installed and old one hauled away as of 1/30/24. It was a long long journey and unnecessarily frustrating!The dishwasher has been working well. I went to return some extra hoses, the Bosch dishwasher power cord and the unfit connector. At return, they told me that the power cord and connector that I was returning don't match the items in my receipt!!!!!! I thought the only thing what was smooth in this process was delivery, but it turned out that they delivered the WRONG items!!!!!! The only thing that was right is the LG dishwasher itself. After having my experience, I think Lowe's owe it to us and tell us what areas they should improve!!

So I came home to purchase the LG dishwasher and haul away online on 11/26/23. I also filled out the online form for installation. Lowe's should state on the website for anyone who would like installation service they MUST go into the store to complete the contract. The website description made it sound like the installation purchase could be made online, but in fact it is not, at least in my state NJ. There is no use filling out the online interest form, since the follow up was not guaranteed. Days after I submitted the online form, a woman called and I asked her to call back in an hour as I was in a meeting. Then she never called back! I was waiting and waiting a couple more days then I decided to go into the store and ask about the installation. The store associate told me that you still have to come into the store the sign the installation contract, which could only be done in person. The frustrating thing is that because of all the waiting to be followed up, later I realized that my installation purchase date is over the installation rebate period. Initially I thought we qualify for the installation rebate when we were telling an associate to buy the dishwasher we wanted, but in the end this whole unclear information made us disqualified from the installation rebate, costing me extra $239 out of pocket to pay for the installation. New dishwasher was delivered 12/22/23, along with the recommended bundle to purchase online, a Bosch dishwasher power cord and a water supply hose/connector for dishwasher. The new dishwasher was settled in my dinning room since we live an apartment. Finally we got the dishwasher, haul away and installation all purchased. We were scheduled the installation appointment for 12/26/23. The scheduling person said we only have installation, but no haul away. Since I purchased the dishwasher and haul away online, haul away is now with Lowe's, but their installation is with their contractors! The scheduling person advised me to call Lowe's to transfer the haul away to the contracting company, so installation and haul away can take place together. So I call my Lowe's store. The store associate said they will have Lowe's people come in the morning of my installation date to take away the old dishwasher, so that the contractor could install the new one, no haul away transfer. We moved things out and got the space ready for installation. Morning of 12/26/23, I received a call from the contracting company saying that they can't come due to some technical problem. Installation appointment changed to 12/29/23. I immediately called my Lowe's store to tell them about the appointment change so that their haul away people don't just take our existing dishwasher out. When I explained the situation to the associate who took my call, he was clearly unaware of someone would be coming in for the haul away for us on 12/26/23. He understood and agreed that transferring the haul away to contracting company would make more sense. So he said he would take care of the haul away transfer for me, but their computer is running slow at the moment of call. So he said he promised he would do it for me later. I didn't hear back from the store, but I received an email from their installation scheduling team saying that our dishwasher installation + haul away appointment is scheduled to 1/10/24! I didn't know what happened to my original 12/29/23 appointment, but 1/10/24 was unacceptable because we were hosting a New Year's Eve party. How could we have a new dishwasher sitting in the middle of my dining room! I immediately called Lowe's and they said that in order for the haul away and installation take place together, they had to waive my previous installation appointment and put in a new request for installation + haul away, and there was no such thing as "transferring the haul away". I seriously could not understand why "transferring the haul away" job would make it so complicated. Also the associate who promised to take care of my transferring the haul away request never told me that this would mean I had to give up the appointment on the 29th and to make a new one. If I were informed, I would still go with the installation on 29th, and then had Lowe's people to come haul away the old one. All these phone calls, we still ended up losing the chance to install the new dishwasher on 29th. Due to my own schedule, I later changed the installation + haul away appointment from 1/10/24 to 1/19/24. It didn't matter much any more after we hosted the party with a new dishwasher in my dining room. I got things out and cleared cabinet space again to prepare for installation. On 1/19/24, an installer came. He looked pretty experienced and professional. When he looked at our space, he immediately said that we need a 4-ft drain hose extension in order to reach the drain. He also pointed out the power cord is for Bosch, not LG, but cord in the dishwasher should work with our existing outlet and we don't need any external power cord. In the end, he could not install for us because we didn't have the drain hose extension. He told us to call again to reschedule when we got the extension. We spent days online and going to different stores to look for a 4-ft drain hose extension. There is no such thing as 4-ft drain hose extension! The shortest is 6-ft! We got a bunch of different hoses and hose extensions, and finally rescheduled the appointment to 2/3/24. I contacted the contracting company to make sure the hoses we got would work, not like the 19th. It was good that the contracting company moved our appointment up to 1/30/24. Finally an installer came and installed the new dishwasher on the 30th. He pointed out the dishwasher connector that Lowe's bundled and delivered to us was much bigger for our LG dishwasher! Thank God he was able to use the connector from the old dishwasher. He used the 6-ft drain hose extension. Although there is a little U shape, I was able to fix it myself later. Finally and finally, we have our new LG dishwasher installed and old one hauled away as of 1/30/24. It was a long long journey and unnecessarily frustrating! The dishwasher has been working well. I went to return some extra hoses, the Bosch dishwasher power cord and the unfit connector. At return, they told me that the power cord and connector that I was returning don't match the items in my receipt! I thought the only thing what was smooth in this process was delivery, but it turned out that they delivered the WRONG items! The only thing that was right is the LG dishwasher itself. After having my experience, I think Lowe's owe it to us and tell us what areas they should improve!

Quiet, very efficient, washes perfectly and the dishes come out sparkling and dries even pots and utensils soiled with a hard, burnt crust! My old Bosch dishwasher, 10 years old, had problems with "e:15" leaks and sometimes the detergent tablet did not dissolve or only partially dissolved. My wife didn't want me to spend a penny to have it looked at by a technician and repaired and wanted to replace it instead. After research and investigation I understood that the source of the problems we had with the old one ultimately came from the improper use of our dishwasher which impaired its performance, disrupted its washing cycle because of the dishes always well rinsed (under penalty of harsh reprimands from my partner!) that we put in them (yes, find out the reasons that the manufacturer and the Finish detergent company advise you not to rinse the dishes before putting them in the dishwasher) and shortcomings in its installation in the plumbing for the water drain which was not done well. I know that now because my new dishwasher reacts the same with water remaining inside the filter and since it is brand new, I know that it is not the dishwasher that is faulty! I also made a service call to the administration of my building so that their plumber could come back and redo the job of installing the water drain which he did not install exactly as the Bosch guide shows. . Now I have taken back control of managing the dishes intended for the dishwasher and don't let anyone rinse their dishes before putting them in the dishwasher! And I hold my own, whether the girls and women in the house (I'm the only man) shun me (out of pride) or not!
Comments (Original): [ Remplacement de mon vieux lave-vaisselle SHX5ER55U ] || ---------------- || (This review was collected as part of a promotion.) Tout nouveau, tout beau, ce nouveau modèle modernisé à ce qu'il faut pour nous plaire comme mon ancien. Silencieux, très efficace, lave à la perfection et la vaisselle sort étincelante et sèche même les chaudrons et ustensiles souillé d'une croûte dure, collé brûlée!  Mon ancien lave-vaisselle Bosch âgé de 10 ans avait des problèmes de fuite 'e:15' et quelques fois la tablette de détergent ne se dissoudait pas ou en partie. Ma femme ne voulait pas que je dépense un sous pour le faire examiner par un technicien et le faire réparer et voulait plutôt le remplacer. Après des recherches et investigation j'ai compris que la source des problèmes qu'on a eu avec l'ancien, relèvent finalement de la mauvaise utilisation de notre lave-vaisselle qui altèrait sa performance, déréglais son cycle de lavage à cause de la vaisselle toujours bien rincé (sous peine de réprimandes sevère de ma conjointe!) qu'on y mettait dedans (oui, renseignez-vous sur les raisons que le fabriquant et la compagnie de détergent Finish vous avise de ne pas rincer la vaisselle avant de la mettre au lave vaisselle) et de lacunes de son installation à la plomberie pour la vidange d'eau qui ne se faisait pas bien. Ça je le sais maintenant car mon nouveau lave-vaisselle réagit pareil avec de l'eau qui reste à l'intérieur niveau filtre et puisqu'il est flambant neuf, je sais que ce n'est pas le lave-vaisselle qui fait défaut! J'ai d'ailleurs fait un appel de service à l'administration de mon immeuble pour que leur plombier revienne refaire la job d'installation du renvois d'eau qu'il n'a pas installé exactement comme le guide de Bosch le montre.  Maintenant j'ai repris le contrôle de la gestion de la vaisselle destiné au lave-vaisselle et ne laisse personne rincer sa vaisselle avant de la mettre au lave-vaisselle! Et je tiens mon bout, que les filles et femmes de la maison (j'suis le seul homme) me boudent (par orgueil)ou non!

Comments (English): [ Not the dishwasher for you if you have a baby ] || ---------------- || I know that Wirecutter named this the best dishwasher money can buy, but I hate it with the fire of a thousand suns. Specifically, I absolutely would not recommend this dishwasher if you have a baby or small children because its ability to dry plastic is very poor. So, unless you want to spend a lot of time hand-drying wet bottles, sippy cups, tupperware, or what have you, I'd look into something else.My biggest complaint with the Bosch is I felt like I couldn't fit many dishes in it. I've read that loading it takes some getting used to, but I didn't get the hang of it after three months - it seems over-optimized. My dishes also emerged still dirty more than a few times. I previously had an ancient Maytag and I ended up exchanging the Bosch for a new Maytag (Wirecutter's #2 pick) which I like much better. The one thing I will say about the Bosch is it is VERY quiet. You could barely tell it's running. But, my new dishwasher has basically the same level of noise and I can actually fit stuff in it so I don't have to run the dishwasher every day anymore. I have never returned an appliance before but this one had to go.

I'd give it 3 stars for performance as the cycles take longer and it dries about as well as our last GE dishwasher (a less expensive model which lasted 13 years). We still have to towel off some dishes; I would have expected more with "dry boost". The 3rd rack is a nice feature for serving spoons and spatulas, but items tend to dry the least up there. The dishwasher is very quiet though. We haven't noticed a major difference between using heavy, sani, dry boost - all the full power settings turned on - except that it takes a couple hours longer, so we've settled on mainly using the normal cycle setting. We've only had the dishwasher for 3 weeks, so we'll see how it holds up.

Sentence (English): All new, all beautiful, this new modernized model has what it takes to please us like my old one.
Comments (English): [ Replacing my old SHX5ER55U dishwasher ] || ---------------- || All new, all beautiful, this new modernized model has what it takes to please us like my old one. Quiet, very efficient, washes perfectly and the dishes come out sparkling and dries even pots and utensils soiled with a hard, burnt-on crust! My old Bosch dishwasher, 10 years old, had problems with "e:15" leaks and sometimes the detergent tablet did not dissolve or only partially dissolved. My wife didn't want me to spend a penny to have it looked at by a technician and repaired and wanted to replace it instead. After research and investigation I understood that the source of the problems we had with the old one ultimately came from the improper use of our dishwasher which impaired its performance, disrupted its washing cycle because of the dishes always well rinsed (under penalty of harsh reprimands from my partner!) that we put in them (yes, find out the reasons that the manufacturer and the Finish detergent company advise you not to rinse the dishes before putting them in the dishwasher) and shortcomings in its installation in the plumbing for the water drain which was not done well. I know that now because my new dishwasher reacts the same with water remaining inside the filter and since it is brand new, I know that it is not the dishwasher that is faulty! I also made a service call to the administration of my building so that their plumber could come back and redo the job of installing the water drain which he did not install exactly as the Bosch guide shows. . Now I have taken back control of managing the dishes intended for the dishwasher and don't let anyone rinse their dishes before putting them in the dishwasher! And I hold my own, whether the girls and women in the house (I'm the only man) shun me (out of pride) or not!
Comments (Original): [ Remplacement de mon vieux lave-vaisselle SHX5ER55U ] || ---------------- || Tout nouveau, tout beau, ce nouveau modèle modernisé à ce qu'il faut pour nous plaire comme mon ancien. Silencieux, très efficace, lave à la perfection et la vaisselle sort étincelante et sèche même les chaudrons et ustensiles souillé d'une croûte dure, collé brûlée!  Mon ancien lave-vaisselle Bosch âgé de 10 ans avait des problèmes de fuite 'e:15' et quelques fois la tablette de détergent ne se dissoudait pas ou en partie. Ma femme ne voulait pas que je dépense un sous pour le faire examiner par un technicien et le faire réparer et voulait plutôt le remplacer. Après des recherches et investigation j'ai compris que la source des problèmes qu'on a eu avec l'ancien, relèvent finalement de la mauvaise utilisation de notre lave-vaisselle qui altèrait sa performance, déréglais son cycle de lavage à cause de la vaisselle toujours bien rincé (sous peine de réprimandes sevère de ma conjointe!) qu'on y mettait dedans (oui, renseignez-vous sur les raisons que le fabriquant et la compagnie de détergent Finish vous avise de ne pas rincer la vaisselle avant de la mettre au lave vaisselle) et de lacunes de son installation à la plomberie pour la vidange d'eau qui ne se faisait pas bien. Ça je le sais maintenant car mon nouveau lave-vaisselle réagit pareil avec de l'eau qui reste à l'intérieur niveau filtre et puisqu'il est flambant neuf, je sais que ce n'est pas le lave-vaisselle qui fait défaut! J'ai d'ailleurs fait un appel de service à l'administration de mon immeuble pour que leur plombier revienne refaire la job d'installation du renvois d'eau qu'il n'a pas installé exactement comme le guide de Bosch le montre.  Maintenant j'ai repris le contrôle de la gestion de la vaisselle destiné au lave-vaisselle et ne laisse personne rincer sa vaisselle avant de la mettre au lave-vaisselle! Et je tiens mon bout, que les filles et femmes de la maison (j'suis le seul homme) me boudent (par orgueil)ou non!

Sentence (English): I enjoy cooking at home.
Comments (English): [ I recommend it for its clean design and satisfactory performance! ] || ---------------- || I enjoy cooking at home. I spend more time washing dishes than cooking, so I decided to escape the dishwashing hell and buy a dishwasher! Before purchasing, I searched and compared various brands, functions, prices, and things to keep in mind when purchasing a dishwasher. In particular, I first saw the Media brand on Coupang, so I searched in various ways. It was a larger Chinese brand than I thought, and it was a company that did OEM for various companies other than the Media brand. I decided to purchase it assuming that other companies would have done a lot of verification on my behalf ^^ One important thing I considered was the AS. The remaining electricity and water bills were so low (it is said that water is actually saved more than washing dishes by hand), so I didn't really consider it. It's very easy to use. The tray is large, so you can fit most frying pans and pots, and it was nice that there was a cutlery holder so you could wash them separately. The basic operating time is 90 minutes, but you can set the timer (there are various courses such as strong, standard, eco, glass, quick, and larva). It's a new world where you just press a few buttons and it's done. I thought a lot about buying it sooner. The interior is all stainless steel, so it's neat. It's much more durable than plastic. I also liked the automatic door opening function. Since the dishes are washed in hot water, they dry really well just by opening the door. The reason I chose the media brand is because the price is great. The functions are not much different from those of major brands, but I was really surprised that the price is less than half. Comments (English): [ Looks Nice, Not Good at its Job ] || ---------------- || We bought this dishwasher to complete our GE Cafe appliance set and it has been somewhat of a letdown. We are regularly having to re-wash dishes and it does not take liquid detergent. It's possible that the poor cleaning results are due to the powder or pod requirement, but our old Frigidaire did a better job cleaning dishes. The two level feature is nice. We can run one load while still catching the stragglers in the other load. If you manage your expectations on pure performance, this is a fine dishwasher. If you expect top notch performance, this isn't the product for you.

Sentence (English): I have had this dishwasher since November 2023, so I cannot yet comment on its long-term reliability but to date (Feb '24) I am extremely satisfied with its performance and abilities.
Comments (English): [ 11.ii. 24 Review: Bosch 300 Series DW SHE53C82N ] || ---------------- || I have had this dishwasher since November 2023, so I cannot yet comment on its long-term reliability but to date (Feb '24) I am extremely satisfied with its performance and abilities. I don't really use the HomeConnect feature too often as I like to open it at the end of the cycle to aid in drying time. I find it easy to load, and I am a cook so often there are pieces of the food processor or stock pots or the blender and plenty of room to fit them all in. The adjustable second rack is great and the upper large utensil and silverware drawer is great. I have yet to use the lower, removable, silverware caddy as the upper drawer/rack seems to handle my needs for flatware and large utensils. The DW is very quiet at 46 dB and it's easy to watch TV, listen to music, or watch YouTube on my laptop while it runs in the next room. I did a good deal of research prior to my purchase and as long as it continues to perform as it is and stays reliable I can easily give it 5 stars or a 5 out of 5 rating for now.

Sentence (English): This item was purchased on a tight budget.
Comments (English): [ Great Budget Option ] || ---------------- || This item was purchased on a tight budget. Got on sale. The unit was relatively easy to install with no issues. I recycled the sound blanket from my old dishwasher, so the operation was nice and quiet. I have used it 3 times so far, and have always used the Heavy Duty cycle. The dishes came out perfectly clean each time, and completely dry. I saw some mixed reviews on bad drying capabilities, but I did not experience this with my unit when using the HD cycle, and when dishes and silverware were loaded properly per instruction materials. It possesses basic features, but that's exactly what I was looking for. I find the more bells and whistles an item has, the more opportunity for things to fail. If you like “over engineered”appliances, you will probably be unhappy with this unit. I can not attest to reliability or longevity as it's less than a month old, but hopefully it will last.

So until I could get my plumber to install, this dishwasher sat in my kitchen. And when it was installed, it was more than $200. When I called customer service again -they gave me the additional money - but I was told that I shouldn't buy appliances during or around the holidays? The third rack at the top adds much more space for glasses, knives and cooking utensils, and it does not take away from the space below for the bottom and middle racks because the interior floor is lower than the old machine. I have been afraid the upward creeping requirements on appliance efficiency will eventually take away heat dry and other features that make these machines really useful.
